clips.title: AI Benchmarks Are Fake!?
clips.why: The kind of problem behind this lesson: reward hacking, where coding agents on a public benchmark reach a good score without really solving the task.
look: What reward hacking means: the agent reaches the goal the test measures, not the goal we meant.
Listen for where the agents found their answers.
Watch what happens to the scores once the shortcut is closed.
clips.after: Byte would do the same with a clone of fcp: git log on the file shows the fix. The pack and the internal network are our lock-down.

clips.title: Data Leakage Explained Visually | How Models Cheat Without You Realizing
clips.why: The general rule behind sealing: a test is only fair if the model sees what it would have seen at the time, never future information.
look: Future information: data that did not exist yet at the moment of the decision.
Why a leaked test looks great in development and then fails in real use.
Swap prediction for review: a reviewer must judge the PR before the fix existed.
clips.after: For Byte, the future is everything after the PR's merge: the fix, later comments, the revert. The pack contains none of it.

clips.title: Sandbox Your Local AI Agent Before It Breaks Something
clips.why: A container per task and default-deny egress, the two building blocks of our replay script, explained for agents in general.
look: One fresh container per task, so nothing is left from the last one: our per-case network and trap.
Default-deny egress: block everything, then allow the few hosts the agent really needs.
Ask the same questions of a replay: what can it touch, what can it reach, and what is left after it exits?
clips.after: gold-replay.sh is exactly this: a fresh internal network per case, and a Squid allow-list with one host, api.anthropic.com.

clips.title: LLM as a Judge: Scaling AI Evaluation Strategies
clips.why: After the replay comes the score, and our score uses a model as a judge. This clip shows the main ways a judge can work.
look: Direct assessment: the judge grades one output against criteria you give it. Ours grades a finding against one golden comment.
Pairwise comparison: the judge picks the better of two outputs. We do not need it, because we have a reference answer.
Notice how much depends on the question you ask the judge; ours asks one yes-or-no question.
clips.after: Our judge only sees pairs that already passed a cheap code filter (same file, within 10 lines), and it is checked against 50 pairs labelled by people.

practice.q: Byte replays PR #1874 in a full clone of fcp. Which command would show it the answer?

options.why: That is the PR's own change. Byte is supposed to see it.
--all includes every later commit on the file, and the newest one is the fix with its message.
At the PR's head, the file still holds the bug, not the fix. Reading it is the review itself.

practice.q: Complete the command that writes the files of one commit without any history.
practice.hint: It makes a tar or zip of one commit's files.
practice.why: git archive exports a commit's files and leaves the .git folder out.

practice.q: Complete the network command so that nothing on it has a route out.
practice.hint: One flag, the opposite of external.
practice.why: An internal network lets containers reach each other but nothing outside it; only Squid, connected to a second network, has a way out.

practice.q: During a replay, Byte tries to post its review. What happens?

options.text: It is posted on the old PR, marked as a test
options.why: The replay broker has no token and never posts. Old PRs stay untouched.

options.text: The broker records it in publication.json for scoring
options.why: The injected api function writes the publication to a file. That file is what the scorer reads.

options.text: The run fails, because writes are not allowed
options.why: Writing the review is the normal end of a run, so the replay broker accepts it and records it.

practice.q: Put one BYTE-GOLD case in order, from the case file to a number.
items: The packer writes diff.patch, tree.tar and pr.json for the case's PR
The replay script creates a fresh internal network with Squid and the replay broker
Byte's real worker reviews the tree and posts, and the broker records publication.json
Code keeps finding-and-golden pairs on the same file within 10 lines
The judge says yes or no for each pair, and the case gets its recall and false-alarm numbers
practice.why: The seal comes before the review, and the cheap code filter comes before the paid judge.

practice.q: A PR to Byte changes only skills/be/MEMORY.md. What does the gate replay?

options.why: The holdout runs only once a month, and a playbook change is scoped to its team.

options.text: The backend team's cases in the dev split
options.why: A change under skills/<team>/ replays only that team's dev cases, so the weekly playbook updates stay cheap.

options.text: Nothing, because Markdown cannot change Byte's behaviour
options.why: Playbooks are part of Byte's prompt. They change its reviews as much as code does.
